headline: The US–Iran war keeps Gulf shipping materially impeded after a US strike on Qeshm on 7 Nov, while Russia–Ukraine strikes continue and DR Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 10,500 confirmed cases.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: US strikes Iranian air defences on Qeshm on 7 Nov; Iran weighs a Qatari bridge-deal proposal to reopen Hormuz. Brent near $98.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: Death toll from Russia's 2 Nov strike on Komyshuvakha reaches 53; missiles hit Kyiv on 7 Nov; Poland's border operation runs to 8 Nov.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI +2.5 for Aug–Oct; record warmth for the date on 1 Nov; CO₂ growth 3.3 ppm/yr; drought threat in southern Africa and Asia.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: ECDC counted 10,532 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,126 deaths in DR Congo to 2 Nov; cases in Kenya and Nigeria; a WHO PHEIC since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: Drone strikes push Sudan's power grid near collapse (AP, 1 Nov); Khartoum accuses Ethiopia of drone strikes on 3 Nov; IPC warns of famine risk.

situations.summary: OAT–Bund spread about 152bp on 6 Nov (OFCE: 163bp on 3 Nov); Fitch outlook negative on 3 Nov; mass strikes on 5 Nov; budget deadline 17 Nov.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation
situations.summary: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov; euro-area inflation hit 4.0% in October and ECB officials signal more hikes.

The S&P 500 closed near 7,377, 5.7% below its 52-week high, and the VIX closed at 25.6 (Yahoo Finance): both inside the Watch band and below the VIX 30 Alert line.

The real-time Sahm rule indicator is 0.00, far from the 0.5 trigger, and the 10y–2y Treasury curve was +0.35 on 6 Nov (FRED).
signals.for_you: The US labour market is still adding jobs; recession indicators are not flashing.

signals.summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September, inside the Watch band; October data due 10 Nov
signals.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). It has not risen for three straight months on the latest data. Brent was about $98 on 6 Nov, down 6% in a month, easing one source of pressure on the October figure due on 10 Nov.
signals.for_you: Higher prices squeeze real incomes, especially for households spending more on fuel and food.

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro-area composite PMI slipped to a four-month low of 51.7 in October, still above 50
signals.state: The final HCOB euro-area composite PMI for October, released on 4 Nov, was 51.7, down from 53.1 in September and a four-month low (Borsa Italiana). Inflation rose to 4.0% in October, a three-year high, as energy costs climbed (Trading Economics). Growth is slowing, but the PMI remains above 50 and no stagnation in GDP has been reported as of 7 Nov, so Normal holds.
signals.for_you: Slower growth tends to show up first in weaker hiring and business investment.
signals.rubric_hit: Composite PMI 51.7 > 50 and GDP positive = Normal

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October; growth near target, no contagion
signals.state: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October, below the 50 line, and the other official indices also slipped under 50 (National Bureau of Statistics, 3 Nov; Trading Economics). Growth was near the official target in Q3, and no new property-developer default wave or financial contagion had been reported as of 7 Nov. Normal holds under hysteresis, but momentum is weakening.
signals.for_you: Weaker Chinese demand tends to weigh on commodity exporters and on firms selling into China.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near target, no contagion = Normal; deflation or developer defaults (Watch) not confirmed

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.summary: Bank of England raised rates to 4% on 5 Nov; euro inflation at 4% adds pressure for an ECB hike
signals.state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock lifts inflation (Sovereign Magazine). Euro-area inflation reached 4.0% in October and the ECB is expected to raise rates into a stalling economy (European Business Magazine). Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency or inter-meeting move had been made as of 7 Nov.
signals.for_you: Higher policy rates tend to feed through to mortgage and loan costs over the following months.
signals.rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma at major central banks = Watch; no emergency moves (Alert)

signals.name: Sovereign debt stress
signals.summary: France–Bund spread about 152bp, above the 150bp Alert line; OFCE put it at 163bp on 3 Nov
signals.state: France's 10-year yield was 4.77% on 6 Nov, down from 4.95% on 3 Nov, against about 3.25% on the German Bund, a spread near 152bp (Trading Economics). OFCE, the French economic institute, put the gap at 1.63 points on 3 Nov, a level not seen since the euro-area debt crisis. Fitch moved France's outlook to negative on 3 Nov. No failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
signals.for_you: Wider spreads raise French government borrowing costs; OFCE estimates about €7.4bn a year by end-2027.
signals.rubric_hit: France–Bund ~152bp > 150bp Alert line

signals.state: Velos Tankers said a crew member of the Velos Sapphire was killed after an explosion on 5 Nov, and UKMTO said a tanker leaving the strait near Oman reported an explosion at the waterline the same day (CBS News). Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two more tankers hit mines in or near Hormuz on 6 Nov, which maritime officials have not confirmed. Gas traders cite the attacks as a continuing risk to Gulf LNG (Trading Economics). Traffic remains materially impeded.
signals.for_you: Expect continued delays and higher shipping and insurance costs on Gulf routes. For travel and maritime security follow FCDO advice and UKMTO notices.

signals.state: The Zaporizhzhia plant has lost all off-site power more than 20 times during the war, according to IAEA counts (News on AIR), and repairs to its lines have been repeatedly delayed by fighting. Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy system continued into 7 Nov (Ukrinform). No damage to safety systems or radiological release had been reported as of 7 Nov.
signals.for_you: Follow official guidance from the IAEA and national authorities; no protective action is advised.

NATO's top commander had warned of possible provocations (Stars and Stripes). No member had requested Article 4 consultations as of 7 Nov.

signals.name: Exploited vulnerabilities
signals.summary: Three new CISA known-exploited vulnerabilities in a week, including SonicWall VPN
signals.state: CISA added three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue in the seven days to 6 Nov and 30 in 30 days, under the 11-a-week Watch line. The latest are a SonicWall SSL VPN flaw (6 Nov), an Apple flaw (4 Nov) and WordPress Core (3 Nov).
signals.for_you: Organisations using SonicWall VPNs should apply vendor patches, following CISA and NCSC advice.

signals.name: Famine
signals.summary: IPC alert warns drought and war are pushing Darfur and Kordofan towards famine; no new Phase 5 found
signals.state: An IPC alert on 13 Oct warned that drought and war are pushing parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan in Sudan towards famine (AllAfrica; Sudan Tribune). Drone strikes on power stations are adding to the strain (AP). El Niño drought also threatens southern Africa. Searches on 7 Nov found no new IPC Phase 5 classification.
signals.for_you: Readers can support UN and Red Cross appeals; there is no direct risk to most readers.
signals.rubric_hit: IPC risk-of-famine alert = Watch

signals.name: Forced displacement
signals.summary: No new event displacing 500,000 in a month; Sudan's long-running crisis remains the largest
signals.state: No single new event displacing more than 500,000 people in a month had been found as of 7 Nov. Sudan remains the world's largest displacement crisis, with millions displaced inside the country and abroad (UNHCR; IOM via VOA). That is a long-running crisis rather than a new event.
signals.for_you: No direct risk to most readers; UN agencies are appealing for funding.

signals.name: Civil unrest
signals.summary: France's large strike day against austerity on 5 Nov; unions plan more action, no deaths reported
signals.state: Hundreds of thousands joined strikes and marches across France on 5 Nov against austerity plans in the 2027 budget, among the largest protests in years (Sortiraparis; Strat News Global). Unions have called further action into December (Connexion). No deaths had been reported as of 7 Nov, so the Alert line of deadly nationwide unrest is not crossed.
signals.for_you: Travellers to France can check FCDO advice and expect transport disruption on strike days.
signals.rubric_hit: Significant protests in a major country = Watch; not deadly (Alert)

signals.name: Humanitarian funding gap
signals.summary: WFP cuts Gaza food aid for 500,000 people over a $450m gap; Somalia and Sudan aid also squeezed
signals.state: WFP is dropping about 500,000 people in Gaza from food aid as a funding gap of about $450m deepens (Outlook India; DevelopmentAid). More than 700,000 people in Somalia lose WFP food assistance in November (Eastleigh Voice). No formal suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country had been announced as of 7 Nov.
signals.for_you: No direct risk to most readers; the UN's funding appeals are listed by OCHA.
signals.rubric_hit: Major ration cuts announced = Watch; no pipeline break in famine-risk country (Alert)

signals.name: UK inflation & rates
signals.summary: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023; CPI 3.5% in September
signals.state: UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in the 12 months to September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band (ONS). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, reversing its easing cycle (Sovereign Magazine). October CPI is due on 18 Nov.
signals.for_you: Higher rates feed through to variable mortgages and new loans; savings rates also tend to rise.
signals.rubric_hit: CPI 3.5% in 2.5–4.0% band and BoE reversing course = Watch

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.summary: Gilt yields steady near 5.15% after the Bank of England's first rate rise since 2023
signals.state: The 10-year gilt yield fell toward 5.1% early on 6 Nov, its lowest since late August, before edging back above 5.15%, after the Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov (Trading Economics). Markets price three more rises by November 2027. No weak auction or BoE intervention has been reported, and Watch is kept while yields stay near multi-year highs.
signals.for_you: Fixed mortgage rates track gilt yields; lenders may reprice deals after the Bank Rate rise. Describes market conditions only; it is not advice.
signals.rubric_hit: Gilt yields near multi-year highs after a BoE hike; no intervention = Watch (kept)

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Cap £1,723; Cornwall Insight forecasts close to £2,000 from January, a rise below the 20% Alert line
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October–December is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household. Cornwall Insight's latest forecast puts the January cap close to £2,000, about 16% higher (Cornwall Insight; Restless). That is above the 5% Watch line but below the 20% Alert line and the £2,200 cap line. Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov.
signals.for_you: Households on default tariffs would pay more from January if the forecast holds; Ofgem publishes the cap by 25 Nov.
signals.rubric_hit: Forecast rise ~16% ≥ 5% Watch line, < 20% Alert
